cards.title: All about you
body: This lesson is about **you**.
Fill in: your name, place, family, school, health, things you like.
And: *When I grow up, I want to be ...*

cards.title: A timeline (Activity 1.1B)
body: A **timeline** shows the important events of your life **in order**.
Tap each year in the example.

cards.title: Make your own timeline
body: List the important events and years of your life.
Then put them on a line, from your birth to now.

cards.title: All About Me diagram
body: Tap each box. Fill them in your notebook.

cards.title: Share and write
body: Share your timeline in a small group. Find the same and the different things.
Then write **10 to 15 sentences** about yourself.

cards.title: Sentence starters
body: *My name is ... In school I enjoy ...*
*My target for this year is ...*
*If I could have just one wish it would be ...*

cards.title: Activity 1.2: a Venn diagram
body: Work with a partner. Put the things you **both** share in the middle.

cards.title: Poem: You Can Be What You Want To Be!
body: Inside you is the **potential** to be what you want to be.
Each day, take **one step** towards your dream.
**Hold on to your dream.**

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What is the message of the poem?
What is your dream?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.q: A timeline shows events:

cards.title: A drama
body: Five learners act a drama: **Please Listen to Me!**
The others watch for **responsible** actions.

steps.text: In Mohammed's shop, **Halima** lets **Rahel** go first. People **wait their turn**.
**Senay**, a boy of ten, runs in and **pushes** to the counter.
The adults call him rude. **Nobody lets him finish**.
Mohammed's **box of oranges** is gone from his car!
Senay had seen two men take it. He tried to tell, but **nobody listened**.

cards.title: Likes and dislikes (Activity 1.4)
head: I liked
I disliked
rows: People waiting their turns (the book's example)
Mohammed did not listen to Senay (the book's example)

cards.title: Think and talk
body: List more actions you **liked** and **disliked** in the drama.
Was Senay right to push? Were the adults right not to listen?
*The book gives no model answer.*

steps.text: A black goat and a white goat meet in the middle of a **very narrow bridge**.
"Go back! I am stronger," says the black goat. "You go back!" says the white goat. The black goat gets ready to **fight**.
The book asks **you** to finish the story with a **peaceful** solution.

cards.title: Activity 1.5: think and talk
body: Pretend you are one of the goats. What would you do to solve the problem **peacefully**?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.q: Why were Mohammed's oranges lost?

options.B: two men took them and nobody listened to Senay

cards.why: Senay saw two men take the box, but nobody listened (p. 6).

cards.title: Family responsibility
body: Everyone in a family has **roles and responsibilities**.
A family responsibility is what you do at home: cleaning, washing dishes, preparing food.

cards.title: Why it matters
body: If one member **fails** to do his or her job, it causes **problems** for the family.
Know and do your jobs to have a **happy family**.

cards.title: Love and respect
body: Showing **love and respect** to your parents and elders is also a family responsibility.

steps.text: An old man sits in the garden with his grandson, who is **eleven**. He asks, "What is that?" "It's a crow."
He asks a **third** time. The boy shouts angrily: "It is a CROW, CROW, CROW!"
The old man says: when you were four and five, you asked me **more than a hundred times**. I answered every time **with a kiss**.
The grandson feels **very sorry**. He promises never to do it again.

cards.title: Activity 1.6: think and talk
body: What can you learn from the old man?
If you were the boy, how would you answer your grandfather?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: The Tandoor
body: A **Tandoor** is a traditional clay oven, common in the **coastal lowlands** of Eritrea. Tap the dots.

cards.title: Tandoor food
body: Food cooked in a Tandoor takes its name.
Bread → **Tandoor-bread**. Fish → **Tandoor-fish**.

cards.title: Tandoor Day in Afta
body: Salih's family lives in **Afta**. Today everyone has a job. Tap each person.

cards.title: Mussa and his grandmother
body: After lunch, Mussa wants to go and play.
Grandmother tells him to **wash the plates**.
"Everyone likes to play, but everyone also has **responsibilities**."

cards.title: What Mussa learned
body: If one person does not do his job, others cannot do theirs.
Mussa washes all the dishes. Then Grandmother tells him his **favourite story**.

cards.title: Helpful or not helpful at home? (Activity 1.8)
head: Statement
Helpful?
rows: I thank my parents for things they do for me
I help my little brother with his assignments
My parents congratulate me on my school achievements
I scold my brother every time he gets low grades
We eat together at meal time

cards.title: Honesty is the best policy!
body: This is the saying at the start of **1.3.2 Being Disciplined**.

steps.text: An old king gives a **special seed** to every young person. "Plant it and come back in **six months**."
**Ali** plants his seed and waters it every day. **Nothing grows.** He feels like a failure.
At the palace everyone has beautiful plants. Ali's pot is **empty**. People laugh at him.
The king says: "I gave you all **boiled seeds**, which would not grow." So honest **Ali** is the new king!

cards.title: Activity 1.9: think and talk
body: List the good and bad behaviours in the story.
Do you agree with the king's choice? Why?
What do you learn from the story?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.q: Why did the king choose Ali?

options.B: Ali was honest and brought an empty pot

cards.why: The seeds were boiled; only Ali brought what really grew: nothing (p. 15).

cards.title: Focus questions
body: What do you do at break time?
Who are your playmates at school?

steps.text: A baby elephant has **no playmates**. Birds say he is too heavy. Fishes say he is too big. Small animals are afraid.
One day a **wild fire** breaks out. The animals run away.
The baby elephant brings **water** in his trunk from the stream and sprays the fire. He stops it.
The animals thank him: he is **a friend in need and a friend indeed**.

cards.title: Activity 1.10: think and talk
body: What would you do if your classmates did not let you play?
What does "A friend in need is a friend indeed" mean to you?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: How they feel
body: Semir likes his friend, but not the **bad things** he does.
After talking to her friend, Sara always **feels better**.

cards.title: Activity 1.11: think and talk
body: Is Semir's choice of friend good or bad? Why?
Which friend would **you** like to have? Why?
*The book gives no model answer.*

cards.title: Summary of the unit
body: Good young people **know about themselves**.
Responsible young people **respect and love** their family.
They solve disagreements **peacefully**, work seriously and **do not cheat**.

questions.answer: From the unit: knows about himself or herself, respects and loves the family, listens to others, solves disagreements peacefully, is honest (does not cheat), does jobs on time, follows rules.

cards.title: A good reader

Reading makes you **intelligent and confident**.

I get information about...

cards.title: Poem: Hello Book!
body: A book sits **shut** on a shelf, like a prisoner.
"I'm your reader. I open you up. **Set you free.**"
"Will you share your **secrets** with me?"

cards.title: Books long ago
body: A thousand years ago, **few people** could read.
Books were written and painted **by hand**.
A good book could cost as much as a **good house**.

steps.text: A queen shows her three children a wonderful book. The first to **learn to read** will get it.
The older boy wants a **bow and arrows**. The little boy wants a **hunting dog**. Reading is "foolish" for princes, they say.
The daughter asks a **monk** to teach her. Months later she reads the first story with **no mistakes**.
She gets the book. She keeps reading and becomes the **wisest and most respected queen** of her country.

cards.title: Activity 2.4: think and talk
body: Did the boys like reading?
Is the question "Why read?" answered in the story?

Food, dress, music, greetings and how we show respect.

lessons.title: Our Traditions: Doing Good for Others

cards.title: Doing good for others
body: Doing good for someone you respect is a good **Eritrean tradition**.
We show respect to **elders** and people in **difficulties**, even strangers.

steps.text: Teacher **Luula** loves a **tifhi**, a traditional jewellery box for gold and silver. One is at Mr. Nuredin's shop.
**Alamin, Sara and Kahsai** want to buy it for her. They do not have enough money, so they offer to **clean the shop**.
Mr. Nuredin asks why. They tell him and ask him to keep it a **secret**.
He gives them the tifhi **for free**. Luula is **delighted**. The children are proud.

cards.title: Activity 3.4: think and talk
body: What did you learn from the story?
Why is it called "The Gift"?
*The book gives no model answer.*

lessons.title: The Diversity of the Eritrean Society

cards.title: Nine ethnic groups
body: Eritrea has **nine** ethnic groups.
Each has its **own language**.
They are grouped **only by language**, not by race or religion.

cards.title: The nine groups
body: Tap each name (alphabetical order).

cards.title: Memory trick: A B B K N R S T T
body: "**A B**ig **B**ird **K**eeps **N**ine **R**ed **S**eeds **T**o**T**e."

cards.title: Living in harmony
body: They have lived together **in harmony** for centuries.
They married each other and shared cultures.
All fought in the **liberation struggle (1961–1991)**.

cards.title: One identity
body: Each group has its own culture.
The common identity is **National Identity: being a proud Eritrean**.

body: Draw nine things for "Eritrea the Beautiful": groups, food, houses, landscapes, music, crafts, sports, railway, coast.

steps.text: Nine families live in a village. The **sorghum** is ready for harvest.
**Quila quila birds** attack Nafie's farm. His neighbour **Ejel refuses** to help: "Not my problem."
Next day the birds are on **Ejel's** farm. Nafie helps him, and **all the other families** come too.
**Working together**, they remove the birds **for good**.

cards.title: Lesson of the story
body: If we do not help each other, **everyone loses**.
Together we are strong.

cards.q: Eritrea's ethnic groups are classified by:
cards.why: p. 37: "solely based on what language they speak".

cards.title: Dawit asks Grandma
body: "What is the use of religion?"

cards.title: What religion teaches
body: Religion can make us **better people**: kind, truthful and loving.
It teaches us to **love and respect** others.
It tells us what is **good** and **bad**.

cards.title: Places to pray
body: People go to **churches, mosques or temples** to worship God or Allah.

cards.title: Respecting other religions
body: Dawit invited his friend **Osman** at **Easter**.
Osman invited Dawit at **Eid**.

steps.text: On Eid morning Dawit greets "**Ma'aidin**". Ahmed answers "**Wa'salimin**".
They tour the neighbourhood saying "**Eid Mubarek**". Everyone gives **sweets and biscuits**. First stop: Sheik Hassen's home.
They spend the rest of the day at the **bride's house**, with Salemet, Ahmed's older sister.
They plan the same fun for **Easter**, a few days away.

cards.title: Religions in Eritrea
body: The two main religions: **Islam** and **Christianity**.
Some Kunama believe in **'Ana'**.
Eritreans have lived together for centuries **without religious conflict**.

cards.q: How did Dawit and Osman respect each other's religions?

options.B: they invited each other on Easter and Eid

pins.text: 1: A revolution is to change an existing government by force and to set up a new system.
2: People revolt when they are unhappy with their government or want to free their country from an enemy.
3: Freedom does not mean we can sit and do nothing. We must keep working, do our duties and fight for our rights.
4: Eritrea was colonized by Turkey, Egypt, Italy, Britain and Ethiopia. The long struggle gave birth to independence.

steps.text: Daud lives in **Habero**. A young **date-palm farmer** was punished for a crime he **did not do**.
He asked to meet the judge. The judge **visited his house**.
The farmer's **rooster** made a terrible sound whenever the **neighbour** came near. The rooster had **seen the crime**.
The farmer was set free and the neighbour was punished. The rooster became the emblem of **justice** in Habero.

cards.title: Our national emblem
body: Our national emblem is a **camel** surrounded by a **wreath** (see Fig. 7.1).
The emblem is put on all **official documents**.

cards.title: The camel: train of the revolution

steps.text: Camels were a **reliable** way to travel. They carry **heavy loads** far and can go without water and food.
Fighters used camels to carry **supplies, food** and **wounded fighters**. In **1982** Nafie's grandfather took his three camels to help.
On the way there was a **land mine**. Two camels were lost. **Gerun** was hurt and lost **one eye**, but he finished the journey.
Gerun served until **independence in May 1991**. Grandfather loved him and cared for him when he was old.

cards.title: Why emblems matter
body: We are **identified** as a nation by our symbols.
Emblems appear on official papers, money, schools and more.

cards.title: The national anthem

body: Tap each date.

cards.title: September 1 (Semira)
body: On **September 1, 1961**, **Hamid Idris Awate** began the armed struggle.
The day reminds us of the **courage** of our heroes.

cards.title: Martyrs' Day (Ribka)
body: Every **June 20** we remember our martyrs by lighting **candles**.
They gave their lives to give **light** to their people.

cards.title: Independence Day (Sherifa)
body: On **May 24, 1991** Eritrea became **independent**.
The armed struggle ended with victory. "Eritrea was **born again**."

cards.title: Women's Day (Ali)
body: Women were **30%** of the fighters. They fought side by side with men.
**March 8** reminds us women's work is **equally important**. Their rights must be respected.

cards.title: Workers' Day (Nejat)
body: **May 1** is International Workers' Day.
Workers help **develop** our country, so their work must be **respected**.

cards.title: Why holidays matter

units.intro: **Rules** keep us safe. We all have **rights**, and every right comes with a **responsibility**.

cards.title: What are rules?
body: Rules **set limits** and **keep us safe**.
They help things **run smoothly**. Rules are needed in **all** activities.

cards.title: Family rules

cards.title: The school community
body: **Students**, **teachers** and the **school administration** together are the **school community**.

cards.title: The Thirty Golden Rules
body: Every school has rules. One set is the **30 Golden Rules**.

steps.text: Biniam and Fenkil (grade 6) love bike races. In **2011** Eritrea was **African champion**. The elders said the races were **risky**.
One day they raced home. They did not see the **traffic light** turn **red**.
Biniam turned onto the sidewalk and was slightly hurt. Fenkil's **brakes were broken**. He crashed into a **woman** crossing the road.
The woman was **badly hurt**. Fenkil spent **months in hospital**. Rules keep us **safe**.

cards.title: Fars, Fathuma and Senai
body: Their teacher said respecting parents is a **quality of a good citizen**.
Senai: "I **listen to the advice** of my parents." Fathuma felt this was **not enough**. They read more.

cards.title: Ways to respect our parents
body: The friends found **four** ways.

cards.title: 1. Do well at school (Fathuma)
body: Success in school makes parents **happy**.
"Wise sons and daughters make their parents **glad**."

cards.title: 2. Be thankful (Senai)
body: His mother carried him for **nine months**. His parents cared for him as a baby.
They **work hard** and pay for his needs. So we must be **thankful**.

cards.title: 3. Care for them (Fars)
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Childhood

states.label: Old age

cards.title: 4. Obey them (Salma)
body: Parents do not want to **harm** us, so we should not **ignore** their advice.
To obey means to **listen** to their advice and **follow** their instructions.
From parents we learn **right and wrong**.

cards.title: Respecting parents

**Listens** to their advice and learns **good and bad** from them.
